facts.claim: A traction elevator counterweight = empty car weight + 40-50% of the rated load (the 'overbalance').
facts.caveat: Elevator World source returns 403 to scripts today; TK Elevator + HSM University re-checked 2026-11-25
spoken: It's built to match the empty car, plus about forty to fifty percent of the rated load

facts.claim: The machine only lifts/holds the unbalance (difference); full car = car side heavier, empty car = counterweight side heavier.
spoken: the motor never hauls the full weight. It only fights the difference
When the car is nearly empty, the counterweight is the heavier side

facts.claim: With an empty car, a released brake would let the car rise and the counterweight fall.
spoken: Release the brake on an empty car, and it wouldn't fall. It would rise

facts.claim: Because the machine is sized for the unbalance (f-0002), a modest motor can serve a full car all day.
facts.caveat: derived consequence of f-0002, not a measured figure
spoken: a modest motor can move a full office of people, all day long

sources.title: Elevator World: 40-42.5% traditionally, 45-50% on newer PM gearless
